import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()

```js
function makeFacadeTextures(seed, anisotropy) {
  const rng = mulberry32(seed);
  const lit = [];
  for (let r=0;r<4;r++) for (let c=0;c<4;c++) lit.push(rng()<0.3);
  const facade = makeCanvasTexture(256,256,(ctx,w,h)=>{
    ctx.fillStyle='#d6d0c2'; ctx.fillRect(0,0,w,h);
    // subtle floor lines
    for (let y=0;y<4;y++){ ctx.fillStyle='rgba(80,70,60,.18)'; ctx.fillRect(0,y*64+56,w,3); }
    for (let y=0;y<4;y++) for(let x=0;x<4;x++){
      const px=x*64+12, py=y*64+12, ww=40, hh=34;
      ctx.fillStyle = lit[y*4+x] ? '#ffe6ad' : '#26303d';
      ctx.fillRect(px,py,ww,hh);
      // reflection
      ctx.fillStyle='rgba(255,255,255,.10)'; ctx.fillRect(px+3,py+3,ww-6,8);
      // frame
      ctx.strokeStyle='rgba(30,26,24,.5)'; ctx.lineWidth=2; ctx.strokeRect(px,py,ww,hh);
    }
  }, {anisotropy});
  const emissive = makeCanvasTexture(256,256,(ctx,w,h)=>{
    ctx.fillStyle='#000'; ctx.fillRect(0,0,w,h);
    for (let y=0;y<4;y++) for(let x=0;x<4;x++){
      if(!lit[y*4+x]) continue;
      ctx.fillStyle='#ffcf82'; ctx.fillRect(x*64+12,y*64+12,40,34);
    }
  }, {anisotropy});
  return {facade, emissive};
}
```

## Objective
- Build a 3D GTA San Andreas–style browser game starring a rooster, with open-world chaos, wanted stars, missions, and more, for the Indonesian-speaking user.

## Requirements
- 3D models and open-world city.
- Ability to cause chaos/rampage ("bisa rusuh").
- Wanted level with stars ("dapat bintang").
- Missions ("misi").
- User wrote in Indonesian; UI/game text should be Indonesian.
- Implicit: browser-playable, polished, responsive.

## Decisions
- Interpreted "GTA San Andreas Rooster" as a GTA-style open-world game with a giant rooster protagonist; title "ROOSTER CITY", tagline "San Andreas? San Ayam."
- Built as a static HTML/Three.js project (no build step), with Three.js r0.160.0 and fonts vendored locally.
- Stylized low-poly sunset city, procedural buildings, cars, pedestrians, police, helicopter, missions, pickups, minimap, touch controls, procedural WebAudio.
- Game runs on port 3002 via `PORT=3002 ./start.sh`; preview verified with `playwright-cli`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vendored Three.js (`vendor/three.module.js`, `vendor/addons/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js`) and fonts (`vendor/fonts/*.woff2`).
- `index.html`: full HUD, start/pause/death overlays, GTA-style UI, mobile layout, import map.
- `src/utils.js`: math, RNG, canvas textures, label sprites, collision helpers.
- `src/world.js`: procedural 9×9 city, roads, sidewalks, merged buildings with window textures, parks, palms, streetlights, billboards, mountains, sunset sky, parked-car spots, mission spots, districts, collision data.
- `src/models.js`: rooster model with animations (legs, wings, tail, peck), human NPCs (ped/cop/gang), cars (sedan/sport/van/police with lightbar), pickups, glowing mission markers.
- `src/audio.js`: synthesized gunshots, punches, explosions, engine, siren, pickups, mission jingles.
- `src/game.js` (~2200 lines): player movement/jump, third-person camera with collision, car enter/exit + arcade driving, traffic, NPC AI (wander/flee/chase/shoot), combat (pistol/punch), wanted stars + police spawning + helicopter, 4 missions, pickups, effects, HUD, minimap, touch controls, debug hooks (`window.__rooster`).
- Browser testing succeeded: menu, gameplay, front/back rooster views, mission start. Only console error is missing `favicon.ico`; WebGL ReadPixels warnings are performance-only.
- Fixed initial issues: too-dark lighting, oversized window grid, hidden rooster eyes/comb, start location moved to `(-210, -42)`.

### Active
- Verifying remaining gameplay paths visually: driving a mission car, checkpoints, shooting, wanted stars/cops/heli, mission completion/failure, mobile controls.
- Screenshot `screenshots/mission-start.png` shows mission HUD correctly, but the yellow mission car and marker are not visible in frame; may need camera/position check.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Teleport near the delivery mission car and press `F`, hold `W`, verify driving camera/speedo and checkpoint flow.
2. Trigger stars via `window.__rooster.stars(3)` or crimes, wait ~3s, screenshot cops/helicopter/wanted HUD.
3. Test shooting/punch, car explosions, health/death/respawn, and mission completion/failure.
4. Inspect mission car/marker placement near `(-126, -42)`; ensure visible to player.
5. Check mobile/touch layout if time permits; then finalize/commit if appropriate.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: page, CSS, HUD, overlays, import map.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: main game logic, debug hooks, missions, HUD, loop.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: city generation, lighting, collision, mission spots.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/models.js`: rooster/NPC/car/pickup/marker models.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural sound engine.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/utils.js`: helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/vendor/three.module.js`: Three.js runtime.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/mission-start.png`: latest gameplay screenshot.

## Important Context
- Server is running in tmux session `game` at `http://localhost:3002`; logs at `/tmp/opencode/game-server.log`.
- Playwright Chromium was installed; `chromium-1243` is symlinked to installed `chromium-1248` in `~/.cache/ms-playwright/`.
- Xvfb display is `:0`.
- Debug API: `window.__rooster` exposes `start()`, `teleport(x,z)`, `stars(n)`, `money(n)`, `mission(id)`, `getMission()`, `setHealth(n)`, `cam`, `snapCamera`, plus state/entities.
- Mission IDs: `delivery` (AYAM GORENG EXPRESS), `rampage` (RAMPAGE KAMPUNG), `hit` (BURONAN AYAM), `survive` (PANIC BUTTON).
- Mission marker positions: delivery `(-126,-42)`, rampage `(210,126)`, hit `(-126,294)`, survive `(126,-294)`.
- Player spawn: `(-210,-42)`; nearby blue car at `(-210,-18)`.
- Wanted thresholds: `[0, 50, 140, 270, 420, 600]`; 4+ stars spawns police helicopter.
- Potential bug to verify: `updateNpcs` iterates backward while mission cleanup may splice NPCs; may skip updates but should not crash.
- Uncommitted changes exist in working tree.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build and refine a 3D GTA San Andreas–style browser game, now replacing the rooster protagonist with selectable cute male/female anime characters, with a free camera and car entry.

## Requirements
- Browser-playable 3D open-world game with chaos, wanted stars, and missions; UI/game text in Indonesian.
- User’s latest request (verbatim intent): camera must be free to look up/down/left/right; character should be anime, not a chicken; character must be able to enter the car; add pre-game selection of cute male/female anime characters.
- Character should be human/car-proportioned rather than the previous giant rooster.

## Decisions
- Replace the rooster player model with `createAnimeCharacter('female' | 'male')`.
- Add two selectable characters: `AYU` (female, pink hair) and `BIMA` (male, blue hair/headphones), default female.
- Add canvas-drawn anime portraits to character-select cards on the start screen.
- Keep the ROOSTER CITY title/city theme, but update protagonist-related text; rooster remains only as unused model code.
- Free camera: expand pitch range, remove walking auto-follow, keep only gentle driving follow; add upward look offset.
- Human-sized character (~1.8 units) so entering the car is believable; reduce on-foot camera distance.
